text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - Taiwan's FGEP group bought a 54,000 tonne shipment of U.S. corn from Mitsui at a tender on Tuesday, traders said. The corn was bought FOB at 58.5 U.S. cents over March Chicago futures, all in one shipment from trading giant Mitsui & Co Ltd. Shipment was slated for February 26 to March 13 from the Pacific Northwest, they said.

SOYOIL SALE - China is said to have bought at least 44,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean oil Tuesday for prompt shipment, export sources said. Some in the trade estimated that Chinese purchases this week totalled as much as 70,000 tonnes. CORN SALE - The Cyprus Grain Commission has accepted the tender of Amiga International PLC for the supply of 18,000 tonnes of maize at $132.75 per tonne. Prices include C & F. Shipment is due out of Limassol in November or December 1996.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC said it was tendering Nov 13 for up to 80,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat, ordinary protein, for Bangladesh. Shipment was for Dec 1-25, 1996. - The CCC said is to tender Nov 6 for up to 10,000 tonnes of northern spring wheat for donation to Ghana. - CCC said it seeks up to 1,600 tonnes hard red winter wheat for Benin. The wheat was slated for Dec 1-25 shipment. CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan will tender Tuesday for 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 soybeans. Shipment is for Nov 15-30 from the U.S. Gulf or Dec 1-15 from the PNW, or Nov 20-Dec 5 from the U.S. Gulf or Dec 5-20 from PNW.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Egypt extended until 1000 GMT November 6 the deadline for bids for 30,000 tonnes U.S. or Argentine yellow corn and 30,000 tonnes of soybeans, any origin. The old deadline was October 30.
SOYOIL TENDER - The CCC is to tender Nov 6 for 13,000 tonnes of crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. The oil was slated for Dec 14-30 delivery.

MARKET TALK - Australia's A$4 billion wheat industry has swung from euphoria to a sense of dread as farmers harvest a near-record crop amid a price slump so severe it threatens a global wheat war led by Argentina, the EU and the U.S.
... Japan is considering re-exporting as food aid the rice it is obliged to import under a world trade pact, Agriculture Minister Ichizo Ohara said on Tuesday.

... Turkey has cleared cargoes of U.S. wheat it was holding up on grounds they might contain ergot fungus and a new regulation will ease a zero-tolerance policy through a government decree expected to come out soon, officials said.

... China has given the green light to corn exports but has set a minimum selling price so high above world levels that the grain is going nowhere and farmers are missing out on much-needed cash, traders said.
... China has agreed with Japanese trade houses to export up to 60,000 tonnes of soybeans to Japan for shipment between December and April, Japanese and Chinese soybean traders said on Tuesday.
... India's soymeal is poised to take advantage of Chinese and Far Eastern export markets as supplies from the United States have eased off and freight rates have risen, traders said on Tuesday.
